thread.title: SEMO agriculture graduate begins marketing career after internship experience
thread.title_full: SEMO agriculture graduate begins marketing career after internship experience

author: First State Times
title: SEMO agriculture graduate begins marketing career after internship experience
text:
Lainey Canning, a recent graduate of Southeast Missouri State University, began her career as a marketing and communications coordinator with Wehmeyer Seed Company in Mascoutah, Illinois, according to a May 20 announcement. Canning graduated this spring with degrees in agribusiness: animal science and agricultural communications from the university’s Department of Agriculture.
Canning grew up on her family’s cow-calf and row crop operation in southern Illinois. She said agriculture has always been central to her life and that she was able to combine her background with leadership, communications, and student involvement opportunities at Southeast Missouri State University.
During an internship at Wehmeyer Seed Company, Canning coordinated large-scale events, managed social media and public relations efforts, and helped create marketing materials for agricultural brands. This experience led directly to a full-time job offer from the company.
At the university, Canning also worked as a student worker for the Department of Agriculture and College of STEM. She created social media content and supported departmental events while holding leadership roles in both the Collegiate Cattlemen’s Association and SEMO Marching Band. “I’ve had some of the best professors and mentors who truly care about their students’ success,” Canning said. “They want to help you grow and connect you with opportunities that can take you far. My journey has been shaped by the people who made SEMO feel like home.”
Canning credited Southeast Missouri State University for helping her build confidence as she prepares for a career in agricultural marketing and communications. “Without SEMO, I wouldn’t have been able to build the experience and connections needed to flourish both academically and professionally,” she said.
The university reports that its agriculture students gain hands-on industry experience along with leadership opportunities that prepare them for careers across the agricultural industry.
